title: Hands up by mistake
setting: At the office, just after a team meeting. Mai stops by Yuki's desk.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: yuki, sakki no kaigi de te ageteta kedo, honto ni yaru no?
lines.ja: ユキ、さっきの会議で手挙げてたけど、ほんとにやるの？
lines.kana: ゆき、さっきのかいぎでてあげてたけど、ほんとにやるの？
lines.english: Yuki, you put your hand up in the meeting just now. Are you really going to do it?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, nani o? kata ga itakute, chotto te o ue ni ageta dake da yo.
lines.ja: え、何を？肩が痛くて、ちょっと手を上に挙げただけだよ。
lines.kana: え、なにを？かたがいたくて、ちょっとてをうえにあげただけだよ。
lines.english: Huh? Do what? My shoulders were sore, so I just put my arms up for a second.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: choudo sono toki, tanaka-san ga atarashii aidea ga aru hito wa, te o agete kudasai tte itta no.
lines.ja: ちょうどその時、田中さんが「新しいアイデアがある人は、手を挙げてください」って言ったの。
lines.kana: ちょうどそのとき、たなかさんが「あたらしいあいであがあるひとは、てをあげてください」っていったの。
lines.english: Right at that moment, Tanaka-san said, "Anyone with a new idea, please raise your hand."

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: uso, kiitenakatta. jaa, raishuu no kaigi de aidea hanasu no, watashi?
lines.ja: うそ、聞いてなかった。じゃあ、来週の会議でアイデア話すの、私？
lines.kana: うそ、きいてなかった。じゃあ、らいしゅうのかいぎであいであはなすの、わたし？
lines.english: No way, I wasn't listening. So I'm the one presenting an idea at next week's meeting?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un. tanaka-san, sugoku ureshisou datta yo.
lines.ja: うん。田中さん、すごくうれしそうだったよ。
lines.kana: うん。たなかさん、すごくうれしそうだったよ。

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: dou shiyou. nanimo aidea ga ukabanai.
lines.ja: どうしよう。何もアイデアが浮かばない。
lines.kana: どうしよう。なにもあいであがうかばない。
lines.english: What am I going to do? I can't think of a single idea.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: maa maa. kata ni sugoku chikara haitteru yo. chotto chikara nuite.
lines.ja: まあまあ。肩にすごく力入ってるよ。ちょっと力抜いて。
lines.kana: まあまあ。かたにすごくちからはいってるよ。ちょっとちからぬいて。
lines.english: Easy now. Your shoulders are really tense. Loosen up a bit.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: chikara nuiteru tsumori na n da kedo.
lines.ja: 力抜いてるつもりなんだけど。
lines.kana: ちからぬいてるつもりなんだけど。

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: jaa, me tojite. de, te o ue ni agete.
lines.ja: じゃあ、目閉じて。で、手を上に挙げて。
lines.kana: じゃあ、めとじて。で、てをうえにあげて。
lines.english: OK, close your eyes. Now put your arms up.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sou. sono mama kata ni chikara irete. hai, chikara nuite.
lines.ja: そう。そのまま肩に力入れて。はい、力抜いて。
lines.kana: そう。そのままかたにちからいれて。はい、ちからぬいて。
lines.english: That's it. Keep them up and tense your shoulders. OK, now let go.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, nanka ii kamo. demo me tojiteru to, nechaisou.
lines.ja: あ、なんかいいかも。でも目閉じてると、寝ちゃいそう。
lines.kana: あ、なんかいいかも。でもめとじてると、ねちゃいそう。
lines.english: Oh, that's actually nice. But with my eyes closed, I'm going to nod off.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: necha dame da yo. hai, mou ikkai.
lines.ja: 寝ちゃだめだよ。はい、もう一回。
lines.kana: ねちゃだめだよ。はい、もういっかい。
lines.english: No falling asleep. OK, one more time.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: あっ！目閉じてたら、アイデア浮かんだ！
lines.kana: あっ！めとじてたら、あいであうかんだ！
lines.english: Oh! I had my eyes closed and an idea just came to me!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kaigi no mae ni, minna de kore yaru no wa dou? chotto chikara nuku dake de, zenzen chigau yo.
lines.ja: 会議の前に、みんなでこれやるのはどう？ちょっと力抜くだけで、全然違うよ。
lines.kana: かいぎのまえに、みんなでこれやるのはどう？ちょっとちからぬくだけで、ぜんぜんちがうよ。
lines.english: What if we all did this before meetings? Just relaxing a little makes a huge difference.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ii ne! sore nara, mou machigaete te o ageru hito mo inai shi ne.
lines.ja: いいね！それなら、もう間違えて手を挙げる人もいないしね。
lines.kana: いいね！それなら、もうまちがえててをあげるひともいないしね。
lines.english: Love it! And then nobody will put their hand up by mistake anymore, either.

questions.english: What happened, and how did it turn out?

choices.english: Yuki put her hand up on purpose to impress Tanaka-san, and Mai helped her choose the best of her ideas.
Yuki stretched at just the wrong moment and ended up volunteering, then a stretch with Mai gave her an idea for the meeting.
Mai put her hand up by mistake in the meeting, so Yuki taught her a stretch to calm her nerves before her talk.

questions.explanation: Line 2: Yuki only put her arms up because her shoulders hurt (te o ue ni ageta dake). Line 3: that was just when Tanaka-san asked anyone with a new idea to raise their hand. So now Yuki has to share an idea at next week's meeting (line 4), and she hasn't got one (line 6). Mai talks her through a stretch (lines 9-13), and with her eyes closed an idea comes to her (line 14): everyone doing the stretch before meetings (line 16). A is wrong: Yuki didn't mean to volunteer. She wasn't even listening (line 4), and she had no ideas at all (line 6). C swaps the two: Yuki is the one who put her hand up, and Mai leads the stretch.

questions.english: Mai is organising drinks for the whole team on Friday, and everyone's in the room. She says, "kin'youbi, minna de nomi ni iku n da kedo, dare ga kuru ka wakannai n da yo ne." Help her out: ask the people who want to go to put their hands up.
questions.ja: 金曜日、みんなで飲みに行くんだけど、誰が来るかわかんないんだよね。
questions.kana: きんようび、みんなでのみにいくんだけど、だれがくるかわかんないんだよね。
questions.romaji: kin'youbi, minna de nomi ni iku n da kedo, dare ga kuru ka wakannai n da yo ne.
questions.answer: Ask with te o ageru as a request: name the people, then te agete. Among friends it's iku hito, te agete! To a room of coworkers you can make it polite: ikitai hito wa, te o agete kudasai.

modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、行く人、手挙げて！

modelAnswers.romaji: kin'youbi ikitai hito wa, te o agete kudasai.
modelAnswers.ja: 金曜日行きたい人は、手を挙げてください。
modelAnswers.english: If you'd like to come on Friday, please raise your hand.

questions.explanation: Tanaka-san's request in line 3 is the classic shape: atarashii aidea ga aru hito wa, te o agete kudasai (anyone with a new idea, please raise your hand). Mai teases Yuki with it in line 17 (machigaete te o ageru hito, people who put their hand up by mistake). The same phrase covers putting your arms up to stretch (line 2, te o ue ni ageta, and line 9, te o ue ni agete). Among friends, o and kudasai drop: iku hito, te agete! Putting your hand back down is te o orosu. Careful with ni and a person: kodomo ni te o ageru means hitting a child.

questions.english: When Mai starts Yuki on the stretch, what's the first thing she tells her to do?
questions.ja: マイはユキに、まず何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいはゆきに、まずなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai wa yuki ni, mazu nan to iimashita ka?
questions.explanation: Line 9: 'jaa, me tojite'. Eyes take tojiru, the verb you also use for closing a book, an umbrella or an app. Yuki says it twice more: me tojiteru to, nechaisou (line 12, with my eyes closed I'll nod off) and me tojitetara, aidea ukanda (line 14). A is wrong: shimeru is for doors, windows and lids, so me o shimeru is the classic learner slip. B is wrong: kao agete means 'look up', with the same ageru as te o agete, but Mai asked Yuki to close her eyes first and then put her arms up (te o ue ni agete). In casual speech you'll also hear me tsubutte for 'close your eyes', and opening them again is me o akeru.

questions.english: It's the night before the meeting. Yuki's shoulders are up around her ears, and she says, "ashita no kaigi, dou shiyou. umaku hanaseru kana." Tell her to relax her shoulders, using chikara o nuku.
questions.ja: 明日の会議、どうしよう。うまく話せるかな。
questions.kana: あしたのかいぎ、どうしよう。うまくはなせるかな。
questions.romaji: ashita no kaigi, dou shiyou. umaku hanaseru kana.
questions.answer: Tell her to relax with chikara o nuku as a request: chikara nuite, or kata no chikara nuite to name her shoulders. With a friend, casual is right and the o usually drops.

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu da yo. kata no chikara nuite.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫だよ。肩の力抜いて。
modelAnswers.english: You'll be fine. Relax your shoulders.

modelAnswers.romaji: kata ni chikara haitteru yo. mou chotto chikara nuite.
modelAnswers.ja: 肩に力入ってるよ。もうちょっと力抜いて。
modelAnswers.english: Your shoulders are all tense. Loosen up a bit more.

questions.explanation: Mai says it in line 7 (chotto chikara nuite), Yuki thought she already was (line 8, chikara nuiteru tsumori), Mai says it again in line 11, and Yuki's idea rests on it (line 16, chotto chikara nuku dake de, zenzen chigau yo). Nuku means pulling something out, so you pull the strength out of your body. The opposite is chikara o ireru (tense up), which Mai asks for first in line 11 (kata ni chikara irete), and a body that's tense is chikara ga haitteru (line 7). Kata no chikara o nuku also means 'stop trying so hard', which suits a friend worrying about a meeting. Rirakkusu shite is the other everyday way to say relax.
